subtopic: Free Fall and Acceleration due to Gravity
stem: An iron ball of mass 3 kg is released from a height of 125 m and falls freely to the ground. Assuming that the value of \(g\) is \(10\ m/s^2\), calculate: (a) Time taken by the ball to reach the ground. (b) Velocity of the ball on reaching the ground.
solution:
Given: \(h = 125\ m,\ g = 10\ m/s^2,\ u = 0\) (released from rest).
(a) Using \(h = ut + \frac{1}{2}gt^2:\ 125 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 \Rightarrow 125 = 5t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 25 \Rightarrow t = 5\ s\).
(b) Using \(v = u + gt:\ v = 0 + 10 \times 5 = 50\ m/s\).
So the ball takes 5 s to reach the ground and strikes the ground with a velocity of \(50\ m/s\). (Mass 3 kg is not needed for these calculations.)

stem: Write the name and symbol of the element from the description: (a) The most electronegative atom. (b) The atom having smallest atomic mass. (c) The noble gas with the smallest atomic radius.
solution:
(a) The most electronegative atom: Fluorine (F).
(b) The atom having the smallest atomic mass: Hydrogen (H).
(c) The noble gas with the smallest atomic radius: Helium (He).

stem: (a) What happens when copper reacts with concentrated nitric acid? What is the colour of the gas released during the reaction? (b) Write its balanced chemical equation. (c) Write the names of reactants and products.
solution:
(a) Copper reacts with concentrated nitric acid to form copper nitrate, nitrogen dioxide gas and water. The gas released, nitrogen dioxide \(NO_2\), is reddish-brown in colour.
(b) \(Cu + 4HNO_3(conc.) \rightarrow Cu(NO_3)_2 + 2NO_2\uparrow + 2H_2O\).
(c) Reactants: copper and (concentrated) nitric acid. Products: copper nitrate, nitrogen dioxide and water.

stem: Name the following diagrams and explain the concept behind them: [two diagrams, labelled a and b, each showing a hand with the thumb, forefinger and middle finger held mutually perpendicular with directional arrows].
solution:
The two diagrams show Fleming's hand rules, in which the thumb, forefinger and middle finger are held mutually perpendicular to one another.
(a) Fleming's Left Hand Rule - used for the electric motor. It gives the direction of the force (motion) acting on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field: the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field, the middle finger in the direction of the current, and the thumb then gives the direction of the force / motion of the conductor.
(b) Fleming's Right Hand Rule - used for the electric generator (dynamo). It gives the direction of the induced current when a conductor is moved in a magnetic field: the forefinger points along the magnetic field, the thumb along the direction of motion of the conductor, and the middle finger then gives the direction of the induced current. (The labels a and b correspond to the two hand diagrams shown; assign by the finger directions in the figure.)
figureNote: Two hand diagrams labelled a. and b., each with three mutually perpendicular arrows (thumb/forefinger/middle finger) illustrating Fleming's Left Hand and Right Hand rules, p-07

stem: Answer the following with respect to the 'Formation of Rainbow': (a) Draw a neat diagram to show the formation of rainbow. (b) Name any two natural processes involved in the formation of rainbow. (c) What does a small droplet of water act as?
solution:
(a) [Diagram to be drawn: sunlight entering a spherical water droplet, undergoing refraction on entering, then total internal reflection at the back of the droplet, and dispersion into the seven colours (VIBGYOR) on emerging out to the observer's eye.]
(b) Any two of the natural processes: refraction of light, dispersion of light, and total internal reflection of light.
(c) A small droplet of water acts as a tiny prism, which refracts and disperses the sunlight into its seven constituent colours.

stem: Name the following: (a) The two metals which can be cut with a knife. (b) A sound is produced when certain metals are struck. Name this property of metals. (c) The non-metallic substance which is a good conductor of electricity.
solution:
(a) The two metals that can be cut with a knife: Sodium (Na) and Potassium (K).
(b) The property by which metals produce a ringing sound when struck is called sonorousness (metals are said to be sonorous).
(c) The non-metal that is a good conductor of electricity: Graphite (an allotrope of carbon).

stem: Answer the following questions with the help of the given diagram [an electrolytic cell: a silver plate as the anode and an aluminium spoon as the cathode dipped in an electrolyte, connected to a cell, with \(Ag^+\) and \(NO_3^-\) ions in the solution]: (a) Name the process shown in the diagram. (b) How does this process take place? (c) Give two examples in which this process is used.
solution:
(a) The process shown is electroplating (electro-deposition) - here, electroplating of silver on an aluminium spoon by passing an electric current (electrolysis).
(b) When electric current is passed, the silver anode gradually dissolves, releasing \(Ag^+\) ions into the electrolyte. These \(Ag^+\) ions move to the cathode (the aluminium spoon), where they gain electrons and get deposited as a thin, uniform layer of silver; the \(NO_3^-\) ions move towards the anode. Thus silver is transferred from the anode and coated on the object at the cathode.
(c) Examples (any two): silver-plating of spoons, ornaments and utensils; gold-plating of jewellery; chromium/nickel-plating of car parts, taps and cycle handlebars to prevent corrosion and improve appearance.
figureNote: Electrolytic cell diagram: 'Cell' at top, silver plate anode (left), aluminium spoon cathode (right), with Ag+ and NO3- ions and electron flow arrows in the electrolyte, p-08

stem:
Complete the following table:

| | Type of the satellite | Function of the satellite | The names of the Indian satellite series and their launch vehicles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| (a) | ____ | Fix the location of any place on the earth's surface | ____ |
| (b) | Weather satellite | ____ | ____ |
| (c) | ____ | ____ | IRS; Launcher: PSLV |
solution:
(a) Type: Navigation satellite; Function: to fix the location of any place on the earth's surface; Indian series: IRNSS (NavIC); Launch vehicle: PSLV.
(b) Weather satellite; Function: to observe and forecast the weather (study clouds, rainfall, storms and cyclones); Indian series: INSAT; Launch vehicle: GSLV.
(c) Type: Remote sensing (Earth observation) satellite; Function: survey and management of the earth's natural resources (land, water, forests, minerals); Indian series: IRS; Launch vehicle: PSLV.
